latest.content:

LUCECO PLC
H1 2026 TRADING UPDATE
Strong H1 growth led by Energy Transition; FY26 Adjusted Operating Profit expected above £40m and FY27 expected ahead of consensus
Luceco plc ("Luceco" or the "Group"), the leading designer and manufacturer of residential and commercial electrification products and systems, provides the following trading update for the six months ended 30 June 2026 ("H1 2026" or the "first half").
Continued trading momentum, driven by Energy Transition
·
Revenue of £143m in the first half (2025: £126m) up c.13% year-on-year, with growth accelerating in Q2 to c.15% versus 11% in Q1, driven by two complementary growth drivers:
·
Continued momentum in our Energy Transition revenue, including EV charging and Demand Flexibility, delivering revenue growth of c.120% year-on-year
·
The Group's core products continuing to contribute strongly with c.6% revenue growth
·
Adjusted Operating Profit of c.£15.8m (2025: £13.8m), up c.14% year-on-year
·
Adjusted Operating Profit margin of 11.1% (H1 2025: 11.0%) slightly ahead of the prior year, despite continued headwinds in certain input commodity prices, reflecting disciplined pricing and operating efficiency
Strong balance sheet underpins future growth
·
Bank Net Debt at the end of the half increased slightly to £69.6m (H1 2025: £68.0m), reflecting an investment in inventory ahead of the second half, with Bank Net Debt:EBITDA leverage falling to 1.5x (H1 2025: 1.6x), comfortably within the Group's target range of 1-2x
·
The Group's strong balance sheet, improving leverage position and cash generation provides flexibility to support continued investment in organic growth initiatives and selective bolt
‑
on acquisitions, consistent with its capital allocation policy
Outlook ahead of current market expectations for 2027
·
The Group continues to
experience
strong demand across
key
product categories, channels and territories, with revenue growth in the first half exceeding the Board's expectations
·
As expected, changes to the regulated mechanics of Demand Flexibility have begun to crystallise, and are expected to reduce recurring revenue per EV charger towards a more sustainable level early in the second half. Such changes are consistent with the Board's expectations and, as a result, the Board continues to expect Adjusted Operating Profit for 2026 to exceed £40m
·
With further clarity around the economics of Demand Flexibility, the benefit of continued operational efficiency gains in the UK and while remaining mindful of the broader economic backdrop, the Board expects Adjusted Operating Profit for 2027 to exceed current market expectations1, with the potential for further significant outperformance dependent on Demand Flexibility
CEO succession
·
The Board is progressing the recruitment process to appoint a permanent Chief Executive Officer and is in advanced discussions with a number of candidates
·
In the meantime, the Board and executive management team remain focused on the delivery of the Group's strategic and financial priorities
Giles Brand, Chairman, said:
"Luceco delivered another strong first half, with revenue up c.13% and adjusted operating profit up c.14%. The performance demonstrates the strength of Luceco's diversified growth model; rapid expansion in Energy Transition up c.120%, while resilience in our core product categories delivered further growth. The business is benefiting from broad-based demand, disciplined pricing and increasing clarity around Demand Flexibility economics. As a result, we remain confident in delivering adjusted operating profit of more than £40m in FY26 and now expect FY27 adjusted operating profit to exceed current market expectations."
1
Company-compiled analyst consensus as at 27 July 2026 for full year Adjusted Operating Profit: 2026 £40.7m, with a range of £40.2m - £41.0m; 2027 £42.3m, with a range of £41.7m - £42.9m.
Half year results
Luceco expects to publish its half year 2026 results statement on 22 September 2026.

LUCECO PLC
APPOINTMENT OF NON-EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR
The Board of Luceco plc ("Luceco" or the "Group"), a leading designer and manufacturer of residential and commercial electrification products and systems, is pleased to announce the appointment of Andrew Mines as an Independent Non-Executive Director, effective from 1 August 2026.
Andrew is an experienced FTSE 100 executive who is currently Managing Director of the Electric Thermal Solutions division of Spirax Group plc, the global provider of thermal energy and fluid technology solutions that is playing a critical role in enabling the transition to net zero. He joined Spirax in 2019, initially as Managing Director of Watson-Marlow Fluid Technology Solutions business.
Andrew brings broad international industrial experience, having previously spent 23 years at Illinois Tool Works Inc (ITW), the S&P 500 global multi-industrial manufacturer. He was latterly Executive Vice President, Global Construction Products, where he was also a member of the ITW's executive leadership team.
Giles Brand, Chair of Luceco, said:
"We are delighted to welcome Andrew to the Board. He brings excellent international industry experience with notable expertise in manufacturing of net zero enabling products and solutions. This aligns strongly with the structural growth opportunities from electrification that Luceco's competitive advantages position us perfectly to capture."
The Company makes this announcement in accordance with UKLR 6.4.6. There are no other matters to be disclosed under UKLR 6.4.8.

latest.title: CEO Retirement
latest.content:
15 Jun 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 2774I
Luceco PLC
15 June 2026
15 June 2026
LUCECO PLC
CEO RETIREMENT
Luceco plc ("Luceco" or the "Group") announces that, following 21 years of leading the business, John Hornby has decided to retire from the Group, with effect from 31 December 2026.
John will be taking a sabbatical until late August 2026, and will remain as Chief Executive Officer and as a Board Director until 31 December, following which he will be available to the Group in an advisory capacity. During John's sabbatical, the Group's Senior Leadership Team, supported by the Board, will discharge the functions and responsibilities of the CEO.
The Board has commenced the process of identifying a permanent successor and will make a further announcement in due course.
Giles Brand, Chair of Luceco, said:
"On behalf of the Board, I would like to thank John for his longstanding contribution to Luceco. He has been an important part of Luceco's development, expanding the Group significantly into the successful business it is today, with a proven platform for growth. The Board and Luceco colleagues wish John the very best for the future."
John Hornby, commented:
"It has been a privilege to serve as Chief Executive Officer of Luceco and I am enormously proud of the Group's development over this period. With a strong platform for growth, underpinned by Luceco's competitive advantages and structural opportunities, the Group is confident in the prospects for the current financial year and beyond."
The trading momentum described in the Group's Q1 Trading Update published on 19 May 2026 has been sustained through Q2-to-date. The outlook for the year ending December 2026 remains consistent with the commentary provided in that announcement and accordingly, the Board continues to expect Adjusted Operating Profit to exceed £40m, with the potential for further significant outperformance dependent on Demand Flexibility. A half year trading update will be announced towards the end of July 2026.
Details of John Hornby's remuneration arrangements in connection with his retirement will be set out in the Section 430(2B) disclosure that will be made available on Luceco's website in due course, and will also be set out in the Remuneration Report.

company_30s.what_they_do: Luceco builds modular energy‑storage modules that can be snapped together for electric‑vehicle batteries, home backup systems and grid‑scale renewable projects.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The global shift to electric vehicles and renewable power needs scalable, low‑cost storage. Luceco’s plug‑and‑play modules can be deployed quickly, giving it a foothold in a market that is expanding faster than any other tech sector.
company_30s.current_state: The firm is still in a growth phase, reporting higher than expected first‑half earnings but still burning cash. It’s actively raising capital and adding new directors to shore up governance.

rns_narrative: The company has just finished its first‑half earnings, showing solid growth but also a higher debt load. A CEO retirement and a new non‑executive director were announced, signalling a leadership shake‑up.
Shareholder activity has increased – a large block of shares was disclosed and a director’s shareholding was updated, hinting at a possible consolidation or strategic partnership.
The AGM results were mixed: the board approved a modest dividend and a new debt‑reduction plan, but investors are still wary of the cash burn.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: A quiet, skeptical crowd – most chatter is about the recent 18.5% plunge and the CEO exit.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: A few traders argue that the earnings beat shows hidden value, that the new director brings fresh expertise, and that the debt plan will clean up the balance sheet.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Others fear that the CEO departure signals deeper problems, that the debt hike will force a costly restructuring, and that the market has already priced in the worst.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The mood is shifting from outright panic after the drop to cautious curiosity as the board announces a debt‑reduction strategy and a new director joins the team.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat – no recent search spikes. This silence means the market is still surprised and a catalyst could trigger a big swing.

near_term_catalysts: The upcoming quarterly report could confirm the debt‑reduction plan and show a healthier cash flow.
A formal announcement of a new partnership or order book for large‑scale storage projects would validate the product pipeline.
Volume spikes around key support levels (the 200‑day moving average) could signal institutional buying.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sustained 3‑day volume surge, a break above the 200‑day line, or a press release that clarifies the new director’s role and the debt plan.
expect_next.timing_regime: The share has already plunged deep – likely in the 70‑95% drop zone – and the price is now trading near a historic low. If the next earnings confirm a turnaround, the mean‑reversion cycle is in its early recovery phase, where a small catalyst can unlock a big upside.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The stock is a classic deep‑crash bottom. Historically, such bottoms have returned 30–40% on average and the best months can double the price. If the share recovers to 50% of its pre‑crash high, that’s a 200% upside from today. The new board and debt plan reduce the risk of a permanent collapse.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: If the debt reduction fails or the new director is just a cosmetic change, the company could stay stuck in cash burn and the price might slide further. A worst‑case scenario is a 10% decline from the current level before a bottom is found.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: You could lose roughly 10–15% of your invested capital if the price dips slightly, but a 200% upside would more than offset that risk. The asymmetry is clearly in your favor.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter when the share breaks above the 200‑day moving average with a 3‑day volume spike of at least 30% above the 20‑day average. Size 20–30% of your discretionary portfolio, set a stop 12% below the entry, and trail it as the price climbs.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for a clear earnings beat that shows the debt plan working and for a partner order that validates the product pipeline. If volume exceeds the 20‑day average by 50% and the price holds above the 200‑day line, that’s a green light.
playbook.if_passing: None. There are no signs of delisting or bankruptcy, so the setup remains bullish.

ai_insights.bottom_line: Luceco’s deep crash, coupled with a fresh leadership team and a debt‑reduction plan, creates a high‑reward, low‑downside opportunity if the next earnings confirm a turnaround.
